Actual fsync success is a reconciled child receipt; surviving-OS process-crash recovery is a separate claim. Linear global percentiles differ from archived nearest-rank per-wave values; no per-wave percentile is averaged. Memory includes one logical wave, scalar latencies/compact peaks and the final teardown manifest; index metadata is reread for final artifact reconciliation.
CPU maxima are per-wave process interval ratios, not instantaneous or whole-host saturation. RSS/FD/handle are observed sampling lower bounds; unavailable metrics remain null.
Socket bytes include HTTP headers/body, not TCP/IP/link headers, retransmissions, physical NIC capacity or other host traffic. Prepared is not received, authenticated or in-flight.
Prelude projection is not a private/raw database checksum. Cache uncontrolled; no cold/hot or steady-state claim.
All original target misses, Gate0=false and original exit code remain unchanged. At most 200 diagnostic codes are printed; every target-miss ID is retained.

Selector timings compare only client perf_counter_ns observations within the same PID/wave; wrapper timestamps are not kernel syscall-entry traces. Raw readiness-poll scheduling is not stored; no-hold dispatch is covered by source/tests, not independently reconstructed from observed socket I/O.
